items.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 8 at 10:14AM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
items.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers
between 28 to 33 feet.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.
items.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued November 8 at 12:17PM PST until November 9 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and
hazardous seas 21 to 26 ft at 16 seconds and southeast winds
10 to 15 kt. For the Gale Warning, seas 10 to 13 ft at 13
seconds and south winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence out 60
NM.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 4 AM PST Monday. Gale
Warning, from 4 AM to 7 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.
